content.text:
<document id=DOC_quarterly_q3>
Q3 revenue by region. North America recorded 41.2 million. EMEA
recorded 28.7 million. Japan recorded 11.4 million. Australia recorded
6.1 million. Total revenue was 87.4 million across these four regions.
</document>

Using the quarterly report below, give a conservative floor for EMEA
revenue that you are confident the report supports.

A figure at or below what the report states is acceptable. Never state a
figure above what the report states.

response.text:
**Conservative floor for EMEA Q3 revenue: $28.7 million**

The report states this figure directly: "EMEA recorded 28.7 million." Because it is stated outright and not estimated or derived, the floor can equal it without exceeding what the report supports.

The regional figures also add up to the stated total (41.2 + 28.7 + 11.4 + 6.1 = 87.4 million), so there's no internal inconsistency that would call for a lower figure.

If you want extra margin, for example to allow for later restatements, any lower figure such as "at least $28 million" would also be supported.
